summary: Essex County lookout first used in 1912; Aermotor tower of 1917, closed 1988, restored with Friends and DEC, listed on the National Register in 2001, now open with a seasonal steward.

facts.design: Prefabricated Aermotor steel tower with a 7x7 ft metal cab (NHLR); the National Register description gives a steel-frame tower

staffing.status: not staffed for fire watch; the Friends hire a summit steward each season

access.note: Reached by trail from U.S. Route 9; the cab is locked unless a steward is present

visit.trail_note: Ranger's Trail is about 1.2 miles to the summit with roughly 1,280 ft of climb; the Friends have been rehabilitating it since 2011; cliff climbing is limited during peregrine falcon nesting season

events.note: First used as a lookout site; the roster's first observer starts May 1912
DEC closed the fire tower in 1988; the roster says it was decommissioned at the end of the 1988 season
Last observer entry in the roster, April to November 1988
Observer's cabin burned three years after closure; only the fireplace and foundation remain
DEC announced plans to dismantle the tower; a local organization formed to raise funds to save it
Town of Chesterfield passed a resolution supporting renovation
Renovated and reopened three years after the 1995 announcement, per Wikipedia; NHLR photo caption dates a restoration to 2003 (see resolved_conflicts)
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, June 15, 1998
Added to the National Register of Historic Places, September 23, 2001

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR describes a 35-ft Aermotor LS-40 with a 7x7 ft cab; the National Register description (Wikipedia) gives 40 ft. No height_m is recorded.

Wikipedia says the tower was renovated and reopened three years after DEC's 1995 announcement, which places it in 1998. NHLR records a 1997 Town of Chesterfield resolution and a photo caption reading 2003 restoration. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one date.

notes_for_editor: Restoration year is disputed (1998 per Wikipedia, 2003 per an NHLR photo caption). WebSearch summaries also mentioned 1996 and 1997 from the Adirondack Almanack and Daily Gazette, and 2005 from a Friends blog, but none of those pages could be fetched (Daily Gazette returned 429; pokeomoonshine.org/about returned no readable text), so they are not cited. The steward line on the NHLR page is undated; as_of 2016 reflects the latest NHLR visit report. The brief's 1998 NHLR registration matches the register. Roster quotes were checked against the cached PDF text.
